content_record.title: Exercise's hidden signal: how ROS orchestrate whole-body resilience
content_record.editorial_body: New review maps the precise redox choreography behind exercise benefits, revealing how muscle-generated oxidants travel via extracellular vesicles to fortify distant tissues—and why aging scrambles the signal. Exercise-induced ROS act as signaling molecules, not just damage agents. Mitochondria and NADPH oxidases produce compartmentalized oxidant bursts. Extracellular vesicles carry redox messages to distant organs. This signal is based on Intracellular and extracellular redox signals during exercise and aging. from PubMed. Read the original report for full context.
